messages:
marco: starting onboarding for umbra11b (converted from hf). ran int4 quant-smoke, seeing PPL jump ~18% vs gemma-lite baseline. attaching quick logs. anyone seen similar on headstride variants?
anya: can you paste the eval command and model spec? which rotary/rope params did the conversion tool pick?
samir: eval command was: `python eval_lang.py --model ./umbra11b/int4 --task wikitext --batch 8 --max_len 1024`
marco: conversion infers rotary freq=1.0, head_dim=128, head_count=88. tool reported: "rotary: detected llama-style but head mismatch -> applied headwise-shear shim"
lucy: hmm vocab mapping step replaced some U+200C/ZWJ tokens? did you run the tokenizer normalizer (nfkc)? small vocab drift can blow PPL on summarization benchmarks.
marco: yes used hf tokenizer from upstream, normalizer=none. quick diff shows ~32 tokens remapped to sentinel ids.
anya: ok two action items: 1) rerun quant-smoke with nfkc normalization and identical tokenizer config to gemma baseline; 2) run a rotary-check script to compare rotary basis alignment across heads.
samir: rotary-check snippet i used: ```python
# compare per-head phase norms
for h in range(H):
    diff = np.linalg.norm(angles_conv[h] - angles_ref[h])
    if diff>1e-3: print(h, diff)
```
marco: ran that, head groups 0-11 show 1e-4 diffs, heads 12-23 show ~0.12 diffs — likely the headwise shim misapplied ordering.
ci-bot: :warning: quant-smoke job 1789998888-1 failed on node gpu-14: vmem OOM during batching step (batch 8, seq 1024).
devbot: noted. marco, try batch 4 to get smoke to finish; but keep metrics.
marco: reran nfkc + batch4 + rotary alignment patch that forces head permutation consistent with original checkpoint. results: PPL delta down to +4% vs gemma baseline. generation quality spot-check looks better but some eos hallucinations remain.
lucy: good improvement. still think vocab remap causes EOS drift; can you run small eval with `--replace-unk as-sentinel` and also print token ids around EOS?
marco: doing that now, will post results. if that helps, schedule a deeper bisect on quantization kernels (int4 per-channel vs per-tensor) tomorrow. :coffee:
